is_anopheles.evidence: The study models transmission involving vectors in western Kenya, including Anopheles gambiae sensu stricto, Anopheles arabiensis, and Anopheles funestus (page 2).

reports_target_markers.evidence: No resistance markers were genotyped in this study; the paper is an OpenMalaria transmission modeling study. It only mentions in discussion that 'there are not yet reports of pyrethroid knockdown resistance (kdr) mutations due to the lack of presence of An. gambiae s.s.' (page 10).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No genotype or allele frequency data are reported.

african_field_population.evidence: Entomological and epidemiological parameters used to parameterize the model were derived from field surveys in Rachuonyo South, Kenya (page 2-4).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a mathematical simulation and transmission modelling paper using the OpenMalaria platform, not a primary empirical mosquito genotyping study.

sub_country_location.evidence: Rachuonyo South district, Nyanza province, western Kenya (page 2).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Field data used for model scenarios were collected between 2009 and 2011 (page 3-4, Table 1).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Not applicable as this is a mathematical simulation study with no genotypic data.

supplement.evidence: No resistance marker genotyping was performed; supplementary files only contain model parameters.

assessment.summary: This study uses the OpenMalaria platform to simulate Plasmodium falciparum transmission dynamics and the impact of vector control interventions in Rachuonyo South, western Kenya. It contains no molecular genotyping of insecticide resistance markers.
exclusion_reasons: The study does not report any target insecticide resistance markers.
The study does not report extractable genotype data.
The study is a mathematical simulation/modelling study rather than a primary empirical mosquito genotyping study.
